name: Turn to Face from Zombie
summary: Recovering facing guard after a failed Zombie pummel uses frames and hip movement to keep the knees between the bodies.
description: Guard recovery after a blocked Zombie pummel uses frames and hip movement to keep the knees inside. The basic rubber-guard exchange already faces the opponent.
overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Zombie, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. The basic Zombie exchange already faces the opponent. A turn from a back exposure is a separate situation and is not established by the position name.

The bottom player has broken posture and supports a high Mission Control leg. The top player's hand or forearm is still obstructing the intended arm isolation. Release any wrist, neck or elbow loading before opening the high-leg enclosure. Lower the controlling leg through a comfortable hip angle rather than pulling the foot against the knee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Ben Eddy — the Zombie pummel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzSxFvNA5Uo); [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs).

flashcards.question: Turn to Face from Zombie (bottom): Which way are the players facing before this reset?
flashcards.answer: The basic Zombie pummel already occurs in facing guard; no rear-control escape is established by this node's name.
flashcards.answer_line: Toward each other in high guard

plausible: Same way, with opponent behind you
Chest down beneath a turtle ride
trap: Across each other in a side pin

flashcards.question: Turn to Face from Zombie (bottom): What must open before turning out of the high connection?
flashcards.answer: Release joint or neck loading and open the high leg before changing the hip angle for guard recovery.

plausible: Only free foot; shoulder still fixed
Only grip on the pummeling wrist
trap: Only ankle cross; arm wrap loaded

flashcards.question: Turn to Face from Zombie (bottom): How should the high leg return toward the floor?
flashcards.answer: Use the hip to guide the leg down comfortably instead of pulling the ankle across a stationary knee.

plausible: Knee pinned, drag the foot outward
Extend leg into their shoulder
trap: Flatten hips with high ankle pulled

flashcards.question: Turn to Face from Zombie (bottom): What should move inside as the high leg opens?
flashcards.answer: Replace the high connection with a facing guard barrier so the opponent cannot fill the gap with chest pressure.
flashcards.answer_line: Forearms and knees guard the torso

plausible: Both arms reach behind their head
Both feet trail outside their hips

flashcards.question: Turn to Face from Zombie (bottom): What should stay oriented toward the opponent?
flashcards.answer: Keep a facing torso while the hips make space and the knee returns; turning only the head does not rebuild guard.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulders and hips as knee returns

plausible: Only face, both hips turned away
Only feet, with chest facing floor
trap: Shoulders face them, hips turn away

flashcards.question: Turn to Face from Zombie (bottom): Their shoulder reaches across your face; where frame?
flashcards.answer: An inside forearm blocks the developing crossface while you recover knee room with a small hip escape.

plausible: Behind shoulder with elbow outside
Across their back with hands clasped
trap: At ribs after shoulder reaches head

flashcards.question: Turn to Face from Zombie (bottom): What makes room for the knee after release?
flashcards.answer: The frame preserves space while a short shrimp shifts the hips enough to return the knee between the bodies.
flashcards.answer_line: Hip moves sideways behind the frame

plausible: Pull wrist while hips stay pinned
Turn back, both knees left outside
trap: Slide hips after the frame falls

flashcards.question: Turn to Face from Zombie (bottom): What must a true turn from rear control have first?
flashcards.answer: A genuine rear-control turn requires rear attachment; the facing Zombie pummel does not supply that starting relationship.

plausible: Overhook while facing your chest
Their arm round your head from front

flashcards.question: Turn to Face from Zombie (bottom): Chest pressure fills the gap; what precedes another overhook?
flashcards.answer: Guard retention takes priority when torso space is lost; rebuild knee room behind the frame before chasing New York again.
flashcards.answer_line: Restore inside knee and forearm wall

plausible: Wrap arm with both knees passed
Both hands pull their head closer

flashcards.question: Turn to Face from Zombie (bottom): What confirms that the facing reset has worked?
flashcards.answer: The restored knee-and-forearm barrier, not a head turn alone, confirms the supported guard-recovery checkpoint.
flashcards.answer_line: Facing them, knees and forearms in

plausible: Face turns, chest still pins ribs
Hands free, both knees trail outside
trap: Hips face them, knee stays outside

flashcards.question: Turn to Face from Zombie (top): Where should your forearm stay before the renewed pummel?
flashcards.answer: A useful inside forearm denies the hand-clearing path before the bottom player can isolate the arm under the knee hug.

plausible: Outside on the mat beyond their hip
Behind their back with elbow high
trap: Hand on chest, elbow outside knee

flashcards.question: Turn to Face from Zombie (top): How should you recover the hand without leaving a lever?
flashcards.answer: Coordinate the whole arm so the wrist is not left exposed beyond a fixed elbow while the bottom player rebuilds guard.
flashcards.answer_line: Move hand and elbow back together

plausible: Pull only hand, elbow stays wide
Lift shoulder, hand still pinned
trap: Elbow forward as wrist draws inward

flashcards.question: Turn to Face from Zombie (top): Which movement identifies their next arm-clearing attempt?
flashcards.answer: The under-hand entry is the cue to recover inside arm position before the knee hug covers the cleared arm.
flashcards.answer_line: Their free hand starts beneath yours

plausible: Knee returns low between the bodies
High leg already rests on the mat
trap: Hand circles head after knee hug

flashcards.question: Turn to Face from Zombie (top): When should the elbow return toward your ribs?
flashcards.answer: Recover the elbow through available slack; do not pull against a fixed shoulder in the high enclosure.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulder has space in the opened leg

plausible: Whenever their pummel changes course
Whenever free hand has a solid post

flashcards.question: Turn to Face from Zombie (top): What must release before you raise the chest?
flashcards.answer: Posture recovery follows upper-body clearance; the opponent turning their hips or recovering a knee does not alone free your neck.
flashcards.answer_line: High-leg hold on head and arm

plausible: Only their free foot leaves the mat
Only fingertips leave your palm
trap: Only second leg; first shin tight
